summary: Log repeatedly prints the message "Ticking entity", and finally crashes the game
description: The bug I m just moving around in my jungle world while trying to record a youtube video. Windows that were open are chrome, obs, sticky notes, streamlabs obs, and the minecraft launcher, as well as the game The game will crash after moving around a little bit. Very lagging in the jungle, the log repeatedly prints the message "Ticking entity", and finally crashes the game. Reproduce - Create a superflat world of jungle biome, and fly freely on the world. minecraft:bedrock,63 minecraft:dirt,minecraft:grass_block;minecraft:jungle;biome_1,decoration,lake,lava_lake - Using spawn eggs to spawn very many parrots. - Use the following command /tp @e[type=parrot] @p Here is the crash report: 19w40a: [^crash-2019-10-03_23.59.03-client.txt] Description: Ticking entity java.lang.NullPointerException: Ticking entity at atd.a(SourceFile:407) at akm.ab(SourceFile:301) at akn.ab(SourceFile:228) at akd.h(SourceFile:399) at akm.h(SourceFile:2059) at akn.h(SourceFile:295) at atk.h(SourceFile:34) at dmr.a(SourceFile:165) at bjk.a(SourceFile:648) at dmr.g(SourceFile:136) at das.n(SourceFile:1389) at das.d(SourceFile:907) at das.b(SourceFile:569) at net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(SourceFile:199)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft and create a new superflat world with a jungle biome.
2. Enter the world and switch to Creative mode.
3. Use spawn eggs to spawn many parrots in the world.
4. Execute the command `/tp @e[type=parrot] @p` to teleport all parrots to your location.
5. Fly freely around the jungle biome.
6. Wait at least a few minutes while observing the game's performance and any messages in the log.
7. Observe that the log repeatedly prints the message "Ticking entity" and that the game eventually crashes.
Observed Behavior: The issue occurs when the player is navigating a jungle biome in a superflat world while recording a YouTube video. During this process, the game experiences significant lag, and the log repeatedly displays the message "Ticking entity" before ultimately crashing. The crash seems to happen after the player has moved around a bit, suggesting that the game struggles to process the numerous parrots spawned using spawn eggs. The player can reproduce the bug by creating a superflat world set to the jungle biome and flying around, using the command /tp @e[type=parrot] @p to teleport all parrots to the player. The crash report indicates a NullPointerException related to ticking entities, which appears to be the root cause of the game failure. The relevant crash report is labeled with the version 19w40a, and further details can be found in the provided crash report file named crash-2019-10-03_23.59.03-client.txt.
Expected Behavior: When following the reproduction steps, the game should allow the player to move freely in the jungle biome without any performance issues, and the log should not display the message "Ticking entity." The player should be able to spawn multiple parrots and teleport them without experiencing lag or crashes. The game should run smoothly, maintaining stability and functionality throughout the session, allowing for an uninterrupted recording experience.
